Internal Meeting

Production & Delivery Meeting for ATP short deliveries
Overview
• The team reviewed current production status, inventory, and upcoming deliveries, focusing on the new raw materials and ATP shipment schedules.

Participants
• Stephanie
• Val
• Jeremy
• Teo
• Bryan

Decisions Made
• Run 24‑hour production using the newly arrived material, starting Sunday, without interruption.
• Ship the current FG to ATP today to avoid complaints.

Action Items
• Finalize and send the material comparison report to YD Cho, cc Bryan, to confirm that raw material quality is the source of prior issues not the production
• Monitor production for any deviations; report immediately if new issues arise.

Discussion Points
• Inventory Status: 172 rolls scheduled for completion this month; 36 rolls ready for today’s delivery.
• Material Transition: New material has already arrived and is in use; no current hole burrs experiance so far.
• Quality Assurance: Jeremy reports no issues with the new raw material; confidence that prior problems were material-related.
• Stef toupdate ATP on the dlivery schedule commitments

• With continuous production and a timely ATP shipment, the team aims to resolve material concerns through transparent reporting and proactive logistics coordination.

AMS Inquiry – Cover Tape Discussion

Project Overview
• This is a new project, not a conversion project.
• The customer currently has an open tool with CPAK.
• For the time being, the cover tape will not be paired with our carrier tape.
• The POD will not be shared, as it is not relevant at this stage since the customer will not be sourcing the carrier tape from us.

Usage / Evaluation
• Actual usage should still be confirmed with Procurement.
• However, the current activity is primarily a look-ahead technical evaluation to assess SR readings and other technical aspects.
• The customer does not recommend involving Procurement at this stage due to the technical nature of the evaluation.

Manufacturing Site
• Confirmed with the customer that our cover tape manufacturing site is currently in Korea only, with no manufacturing site in China, Vietnam and Philippines.

Customer / Supplier Information
• The customer inquired whether SST is currently our customer. This needs to be verified with HQ.
• The majority suppliers for TNR are EPAK and Advantek.

Action Items
• Verify with HQ whether SST is an existing customer.
• Confirm the expected usage/volume with Procurement when the project progresses to the appropriate stage.
• Continue monitoring the technical evaluation, particularly the SR readings and other technical requirements.

Discussion on the technical specifications, manufacturing process, and customer relationships for carrier tapes and thermoforming trays used in semiconductor packaging.

Key Discussion Points
Materials
* Discussed the use of Polycarbonate (PC), Hybrid PC, and Polystyrene (PS) materials.
* Hybrid PC offers a more cost-effective solution than 100% PC while delivering comparable performance.
* Hybrid PC is generally less expensive and faster to manufacture because it eliminates the extrusion process.
* Performance of Hybrid PC closely matches that of pure PC and remains within the required packaging specifications.

Performance
* Surface Resistance (SR) performance ranges from E4 to E6, which is equivalent to the current materials supplied by 3M and Advantek.

Tooling Options
* KP Tooling: USD 5,000
* Rotary Tooling: USD 4,000
* Linear Tooling: USD 1,500
* Tooling charges may be offered free of charge (FOC) depending on the customer's forecasted demand and business volume.

Cost-Saving Opportunities
* Hybrid PC provides a lower-cost alternative to pure PC while maintaining similar technical and packaging performance.
* Faster production lead time is achieved due to the simplified manufacturing process.

Action Items
* The customer will provide one initial Part Number (PN), Package Outline Drawing (POD), and estimated demand/forecast.
* Upon receipt of the required information, we will prepare and submit a formal proposal.

Product Offering
Heat-sealing type cover tape.

Cover Tape Structure
* Single-sided: PET layer / Olefin layer / Dissipative layer.
* Double-sided: PET layer / Olefin layer / Dissipative layer with an additional dissipative layer on the top surface.

Technical Discussion
* The customer's current material is specified as single-sided. However, based on actual measurements, the surface resistance (SR) on both sides exhibits dissipative characteristics.
* In view of this, we will offer our double-sided dissipative cover tape as the recommended solution.

Performance
* Peel Value Force Test (PVFT): 56.8 to 80.3, depending on the heat-sealing temperature.
* Haze/Luminous Transmittance: Improved optical performance compared to the previous model (KAH1), providing better transparency.

8D review

Overview
The meeting examined a production defect affecting carrier tape rolls (part KS‑1204-07). Re‑inspections revealed that the carrier tape length was inconsistently below the required 515 m, causing aborted reels and short‑length rolls (e.g., 44 reels produced instead of 46). Root‑cause analysis identified machine counter inaccuracies, lack of weight verification, and insufficient inspection criteria as key contributors.

Decision made /  Impact

a. Replace defective machine counter on L4 machine. / Corrects double‑counting, restores accurate packet counts
b. Implement weight measurement for all carrier tape rolls / Adds an independent check of tape length
c. Update inspection standard to include weight verification and a 0.5 m visual tolerance / Prevents future “short‑length” defects
d. Post net weight of carrier tape products on inspection boards. / Provides real‑time reference for inspectors
e. Add machine‑counter verification to the production start‑up checklist. / Prevents recurrence of counter errors
f. Train all operators on revised inspection form and counter‑discrepancy response. / Ensures consistent application of new procedures

1. Root‑Cause Analysis
   * Carrier tape length < 515 m → aborted reels.  
   * Machine counter on L4 produced higher packet counts than actual length (double‑count).  
   * L5 machine had higher weight and length, confirming counter discrepancy.

2. Re‑Inspection Findings
   * 81 rolls re‑inspected: 63 hold, 18 meet ≥515 m.  
   * Trial lengths: 475 m (weight 2.365 kg) and 505 m (weight 2.476 kg).  
   * Weight tolerance set to 2.52–2.53 kg.  

3. Inspection Gaps 
   * No weight check previously; relied solely on machine vision count.  
   * Inspection criteria omitted actual length with verification.  

4. Machine Setup & Maintenance
   * Counter accuracy verification was missing from the start‑up checklist.  
   * No preventive maintenance record for counter replacement.  

5. Lessons Learned
   * Machine‑counter accuracy must be validated before production.  
   * Inspection standards require both visual and weight checks.  
   * Continuous monitoring of carrier tape weight can flag length deviations early.

Meetign with PHK team regarding Production Issue Review – L4/L5 Machines

Overview
This meeting reviewed production records, identified a counting error on the L4 machine, and discussed corrective actions, verification steps, and documentation requirements.

Participants & Roles
- Jeremy – Factory Manager  
- Val – Sales  
- Jowan - Quality  
- Genniel - Production

Decisions Made
- Machine Correction – The L4 counter was recalibrated and the sensor was realigned. For part replacement. 
- Data Re‑analysis – Production data for March 2025 (L5) and 2026 (L4) will be re‑examined to confirm accuracy.  
- Reporting Adjustments – Reports will be updated to reflect corrected counts and to justify the 475 m closure metric.  

Action Items
- Lot Verification – Identify the specific lot(s) affected (e.g., 0202) and confirm their production data.  
- Sensor Review – Test the updated sensor on the L4 machine to ensure no double‑counting occurs.  
- Dose Justification – PHK will prepare a justification for February 2026 dose counts.  
- Documentation – Send the revised production report to the L4 team and archive the changes.

Discussion Points
- Root Cause – The L4 machine counter was double‑counting, causing an inflated product count.  

- Production Timeline – 
  - L5 production record shows March 2025 with no issues last year.  
  - L4 was used for 2026 production; first issue reported February 2025.  
- Sensor Issues** – The sensor misread counts, leading to double counting; realignment has corrected the problem, but it will soon be replaced, awting for the replacement part
- Comparative Analysis – Skyworks and Amkor used the same machine; Amkor had no issues, maybe because left over is too much.  
- Metrics – The 475 m closure metric was accepted even though actual samples were slightly above 500 m; justification will be documented.  We will accept only for rolls produced starting February 2026
- Future Prevention – Consider machine replacement, prefer to use L5 machine until new part is replaced in L4, though calibration has done in L4 but neeed to monitor counter behavior closely.  

> Key Takeaway: After recalibration and sensor realignment, the L4 machine’s counting error has been corrected. All affected lots will be verified, and updated reports will be issued to ensure traceability and compliance.
